title: Trump Mocks John McCain: 'I Like People Who Weren't Captured'
description_short: Trump Mocks John McCain: 'I Like People Who Weren't Captured'
description_medium: At a July 2015 campaign event in Iowa, Donald Trump disputed Senator John McCain’s status as a war hero because McCain had been captured during the Vietnam War. The remarks triggered criticism from veterans and fellow Republicans and became a major controversy in the Republican primary.
description_long: At the Family Leadership Summit in Ames, Iowa, on July 18, 2015, Donald Trump challenged Senator John McCain’s status as a war hero because McCain had been captured during the Vietnam War. Trump said he preferred people who had not been captured. McCain, a Navy pilot, had been held as a prisoner of war in North Vietnam for more than five years after his aircraft was shot down in 1967. His captivity and refusal of early release when it would have separated him from fellow prisoners were central parts of his public record. Trump’s remarks drew immediate criticism from veterans and political figures and became a defining controversy in the early Republican presidential primary. McCain later said he did not consider Trump’s apology adequate. The dispute put Trump’s attitude toward military service and sacrifice under national scrutiny and sharpened tensions between him and a prominent Republican senator. The episode is documented in a transcript of Trump’s own remarks; its significance lies in the public insult and ensuing political backlash, not in any formal policy change.
